followup_4820.scope: Finite reassessment preserves all 88 source objects, products, reference pairs and earlier index entries. The following assessment supersedes the prior CNOT6/CNOT6L class refinements; no previous source record is overwritten.

16.basis: Human GFP-CCR4b/CNOT6L immunoprecipitation and mass spectrometry recovered CNOT1 with other CCR4-NOT subunits; endogenous mouse coimmunoprecipitation provides additional complex-level support. The positive association is retained. The source does not isolate a CNOT1–CNOT6L binary contact, and the human catalytic-module study identifies CAF1/POP2 as the bridge to CCR4a/b. Enzyme-binding specificity is therefore not added to this source assertion.

17.basis: Human GFP-CCR4a/CNOT6 immunoprecipitates contained a subunit pattern like the CCR4b complex, including CNOT1. This is positive complex-association evidence. The source does not distinguish CNOT1 contact with CNOT6 from linkage through CAF1/POP2, as described in the human catalytic-module study. Retain the original association without an enzyme-binding replacement.

25.basis: The original positive annotation and the accessible GW182 study abstract support CCR4-NOT recruitment; the original full assay was not recovered. Independent human coimmunoprecipitation and reconstitution support the CNOT6L-containing complex, while CAF1/POP2 can bridge CCR4 proteins to CNOT1. Retain the positive association without extending the limited source access to a direct CNOT1–CNOT6L contact or an enzyme-binding replacement.

28.basis: Human GFP-NOT1 coimmunoprecipitates HA-CCR4b/CNOT6L through the NOT1 middle region. The study explicitly distinguishes this association from recombinant binary pull-downs and structures for NOT1–CAF1/POP2, which bridge CCR4a/b to the NOT module. Preserve the CNOT6L association as non-core; the experiment does not establish a separate CNOT1–CNOT6L binding interface.

31.basis: Human-cell coimmunoprecipitation recovers HA-CCR4a/CNOT6 with the NOT1 middle region. In the same study CAF1/POP2 connect CCR4a/b to the NOT module, whereas direct recombinant binding is demonstrated for NOT1–CAF1/POP2. Preserve the positive CNOT6 association without an enzyme-binding refinement from this co-complex assay.

43.basis: The exact PMID:26496610 IntAct record is a positive anti-tag coimmunoprecipitation association in human HeLa cells, represented by spoke expansion from a complex. It supports the CNOT1–CNOT6L association but does not isolate their direct interface. In light of the experimentally characterized CAF1/POP2 bridge, retain the source assertion as non-core without the enzyme-binding replacement.

48.basis: The exact PMID:26496610 IntAct record links CNOT1 and CNOT6 by positive anti-tag coimmunoprecipitation in human HeLa cells and is a spoke-expanded association. Retain that physical complex evidence. It does not distinguish direct CNOT1–CNOT6 contact from the characterized CAF1/POP2-mediated connection, so an enzyme-binding replacement is not added.

55.basis: The exact BioPlex records recover CNOT1 with CNOT6L by anti-tag coimmunoprecipitation in human 293T and HCT116 cells. Both are positive spoke-expanded associations; neither is a binary-contact assay. Retain the reproducible complex association as non-core, without inferring an additional CNOT1 enzyme-binding interface from these records.
